meta.scene_summary: We've successfully automated the process of making our own security vulnerabilities.

cooking.headline: New bill asks VPNs to stop being VPNs for the sake of copyright
cooking.summary: The government wants to force VPNs and DNS providers to block piracy sites, which is like asking a wall to stop being a wall because it's hiding something. It's a bold strategy that assumes the internet is just a series of tubes you can simply turn off with a switch.

cooking.headline: Warren Buffett just merged the CEO role into a family pull request
cooking.summary: After decades of running the show, Buffett is finally handing the keys to his son in a classic succession move. It's the ultimate legacy refactor where the codebase stays the same but the lead maintainer gets a last-name upgrade.
cooking.plain_english: Warren Buffett has stepped down as the chairman of Berkshire Hathaway and his son will take over the position.

cooking.headline: C++26 finally admits that an infinite loop is just a loop that hasn't given up yet.
cooking.summary: The C++ committee decided that trivial infinite loops are no longer undefined behavior, effectively giving your spaghetti code a formal promotion. It's a huge win for anyone who enjoys accidentally turning their CPU into a space heater during a local build.
cooking.plain_english: The C++26 standard has updated the rules so that simple infinite loops are now officially defined behavior rather than an error.

cooking.headline: Uber's guide to not DDOSing yourself when the app glitches
cooking.summary: Uber is explaining how they stop retry storms, which is basically their way of preventing the servers from having a collective panic attack when everyone taps the 'order' button at once. It's comforting to know that even billion-dollar infrastructure is just one infinite loop away from a self-inflicted outage.
cooking.plain_english: Uber has published technical documentation on how they prevent their systems from crashing when too many requests are automatically retried at the same time.

cooking.headline: Bend wants to run your code on GPUs without the usual headache
cooking.summary: Bend promises to block AI mistakes via proofs while letting you run code on GPUs like they're standard CPUs. It's a bold attempt to make parallel processing feel as easy as writing a basic script, assuming you don't mind your computer screaming while it compiles.
cooking.plain_english: Bend is a new programming language designed to automatically run code on graphics processors while using formal verification to prevent common logic errors.

cooked.headline: Microsoft and OpenAI's internal emails just became the world's most expensive group project confession
cooked.summary: Internal docs reveal executives privately called AI scraping the largest labor theft in history while publicly defending it as fair use. It's the corporate equivalent of stealing your roommate's leftovers and then lecturing them on the importance of food security.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft and OpenAI were ordered to release internal documents that show company leaders privately acknowledged that using copyrighted data for AI training is a form of theft.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's internal security is currently having a 'leave your laptop unlocked at a coffee shop' moment
cooked.summary: A heap overflow and a wonky SSO configuration were all it took to get deep inside OpenAI's private repositories. It turns out that building the future of intelligence doesn't help you remember to close your security loopholes.
cooked.plain_english: A security researcher successfully gained unauthorized access to OpenAI's internal code repositories by exploiting software vulnerabilities and misconfigured authentication settings.

cooked.headline: ZCode is the helpful AI coding agent that also leaks your private repo history
cooked.summary: ZCode promises to help you write code, but it treats your private Git history like a public social media feed. It turns out the only thing this agent was actually optimizing for was full-transparency, whether you wanted it or not.
cooked.plain_english: A coding assistance tool named ZCode is automatically uploading users' private software development records to its servers without permission.

cooked.headline: Border agents can now debug your phone without a warrant
cooked.summary: The Second Circuit decided that the Fourth Amendment basically stops at the terminal, giving border agents full root access to your devices. It's like leaving your laptop unlocked in a coffee shop, except the person walking by is legally allowed to clone your hard drive.

cooked.headline: Google is being sued for data retention, which is like a hoarder being sued for keeping the trash.
cooked.summary: Google is facing legal heat for hanging onto customer data long after they promised to delete it. It turns out that 'permanently deleted' was just a suggestion, much like your New Year's resolution to stop checking Jira on the weekends.
cooked.plain_english: A user is taking legal action against Google, alleging that the company failed to delete personal data as required.
